"Implement the solution in src/main/java/SimpleLinkedList.java so that the tests in src/test/java/SimpleLinkedListTest.java pass. The specification follows.

# Instructions

Write a prototype of the music player application.

For the prototype, each song will simply be represented by a number.
Given a range of numbers (the song IDs), create a singly linked list.

Given a singly linked list, you should be able to reverse the list to play the songs in the opposite order.

~~~~exercism/note
The linked list is a fundamental data structure in computer science, often used in the implementation of other data structures.

The simplest kind of linked list is a **singly** linked list.
That means that each element (or \"node\") contains data, along with something that points to the next node in the list.

If you want to dig deeper into linked lists, check out [this article][intro-linked-list] that explains it using nice drawings.

[intro-linked-list]: https://medium.com/basecs/whats-a-linked-list-anyway-part-1-d8b7e6508b9d
~~~~


Do NOT modify the tests or the build files except as stated below. Do not create new files unless the specification requires them; Helper classes may go only in the solution's package."

content.text: Let's take a look at the test file and the existing solution file.

Simple. Implement the linked list. push = add to head (since pop returns the last added element). reverse reverses the order. asArray returns the elements in list order (in the test, after pushing 9,8,7,6,5, the expected value is {'5','6','7','8','9'} — meaning asArray returns in the order from head to tail, i.e., the order in which the elements were added). The list keeps the head as the most recently pushed element. asArray should return in the order from tail to head (the order in which the elements were added).

Implementation: a Node class with value and next. push adds to head. pop removes head. reverse: iterate and reverse. asArray: collect from head to tail.
Alright, let's run the tests. I'll check the build file.

All tests pass. I implemented `src/main/java/SimpleLinkedList.java` as a singly linked list:

- **`push(T)`** — adds the value as the new head node, so `pop()` returns the most recently added element.
- **`pop()`** — removes and returns the head; throws `NoSuchElementException` on an empty list.
- **`reverse()`** — iteratively reverses the `next` pointers in place, updating the head.
- **`asArray(Class<T>)`** — walks from head to tail and fills an array created via `Array.newInstance`, returning elements in insertion order.
- **`size()`** — tracked with a counter, updated by `push`/`pop`.
- **Constructors** — the no-arg constructor starts empty; the `T[]` constructor pushes each value in order.

The node itself is a private static nested `Node<T>` class in the same package, so no new files were needed. `./gradlew test` reports **BUILD SUCCESSFUL** with all 7 tests in `SimpleLinkedListTest` passing.
